Original Law.Subject: Policies and Guidelines on Streamlining the Bureau of Internal Revenue Under Executive Order No. 430
Original Law.To: All Internal Revenue Officials and Employees

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVE

This Order is issued to prescribe the policies and guidelines in the implementation of Executive Order (E.O.) No. 430 dated July 28, 1997 on Further Streamlining the Bureau of Internal Revenue in line with its Computerized Integrated Tax System.

II. POLICIES AND GUIDELINES

A. On Organizational Structure

1. The design of the Table of Organization (T.O.) or organizational structure of the Services/Offices prescribed under E.O. 430 shall be determined by the following:

1.1 The structure shall adopt the concept of a taxpayer-focused service organization and shall emphasize enforcement effectiveness to enhance voluntary compliance.

1.2 The National Office, as prescribed in E.O. 430, shall be responsible for the development and formulation of broad national tax administration policies and programs and in providing overall direction, guidance and control of the operations of the internal revenue service while Regional Offices and Revenue Data Centers shall execute the national policies and programs prescribed by the National Office for enforcement of the internal revenue laws.

1.3 Regional Offices shall serve as counterparts of the Operations Group, the Legal and Enforcement Group and the Resource Management Group in the National Office while the Revenue Data Centers shall serve as counterparts of the Information System Group.

2. In the preparation of the Revenue Administrative Order (RAO) defining the organization and functions of all Services/Offices under E.O. 430 and the Divisions thereunder, the following shall be observed:

2.1 All functions under E.O. 430 shall be determined according to the process improvement and computerization activities undertaken by the Bureau.

2.2 All functions of Services/Offices as defined in E.O. 430 shall be properly allocated and accounted for in the Divisions created thereunder.

2.3 Common or routine functions of Services/Offices/Divisions shall also be reflected in their respective functional statements.

2.4 All functions of offices under E.O. 132 shall be inventoried and matched against the functions under E.O. 430 to ensure that a corresponding office or application system shall perform the functions.

3. The number of Regional Offices and District Offices shall be rationalized considering efficiency and effectiveness in the delivery of services to the taxpayers and the greater and wider span of control as a result of computerization.

3.1 The number of Regional Offices and Revenue District Offices (RDOs) shall be determined using the following factors:

3.1.1 Critical values of the Regional Offices and RDOs considering variables such as collections, total number of tax returns filed, potential business and compensation taxpayer base, land area and expenditures computed as follows:

a) To compute for the percentages of each variable for each Regional Office/RDO:

b) To compute for the critical values, assign proportions for each variable. The assignment of proportions are: 50% for collections, 30% for total number of tax returns filed, 20% for potential business taxpayer base, 5% for potential compensation taxpayer base, 5% for land area and — 10% for expenditures. That is:

Critical value = .50 (collections p.v.) + .30 (total number of tax returns filed p.v.) + .20 (potential business taxpayer base p.v.) + .05 (potential compensation taxpayer base p.v.) + .05 (land area p.v.) — 10 (expenditures p.v.)

wherein:

Collections — Internal revenue collections by Revenue District Office (RDO) by Regional Office for CY 1996 based on 1209 Reports consolidated by Revenue Accounting Division.

Total Number of Tax Returns Filed — Number of tax returns filed in the Philippines by RDO by Regional Office for CY 1996. Source: Statistics Division

Potential Business Taxpayer Base — Number of establishments based on 1995 data from National Statistics Office.

Potential Compensation Taxpayer Base — 1996 labor force report of the National Statistics Office. Labor force by revenue district for the RDOs in Metro Manila, Makati and Cebu City is not available. Breakdown for these RDOs was estimated by using the data on individual filers for the particular district as basis for percentage distribution of the total force for the area.

Land area — Based on 1990 data from the National Statistics Office. Land area estimates for selected RDOs in Metro Manila (Quezon City, Makati, Manila) and Cebu City were based on the boundaries specified in the RAOs and "visually" proportioned as shown on the map for the particular boundaries,

Expenditures — Based on 1996 total obligations incurred submitted by Regional Offices to Statistics Division (where expenditures for Regional Offices were exclusively for Regional Offices).

Regional Offices and RDOs shall be ranked based on critical values.

3.1.2 Geographical location/relative distance or contiguity of the RDOs to one another.

3.1.3 The political subdivision as embodied in the Administrative Code.

3.2 The final number of Regional Offices and RDOs to be retained shall be determined by evaluating the resultant number of Regional Offices and RDOs using further the following criteria:

a. Span of Control

b. Dislocation of Employees

c. Budget

d. Interface With Other Agencies

e. Internal Recruitment for Revenue Data Centers

3.3 The office location of the Regional Offices and RDOs shall be determined taking into consideration the strategic location of the place and the availability of building and facilities.

4. The T.O. and the RAO for the Consolidation of Regional Offices and RDOs together with the creation of Revenue Data Centers and RDO Extension Offices shall be signed by the Commissioner for approval by the Secretary of Finance.

B. On Deployment of Personnel

1. The implementation of the BIR T.O. under E.O. 430 shall not result to involuntary separation or diminution in rank and compensation of personnel.

2. Staffing under the modified structure shall come from existing personnel. External hiring shall only be considered for highly technical position where the expertise required is not internally available and the need is immediate (i.e. cannot wait for retooling/retraining interventions).

3. Staffing under the modified T.O. shall be done in two stages, i.e., interim assignment and final placement.

3.1. Interim assignments shall be made pending the finalization and approval of a Revised Staffing Pattern pursuant to E.O. 430 in order to avoid disruption in normal operations, mobilize newly-created units and effect a smooth transition to the modified structure.

3.1.1. Interim assignments shall be effected through the issuance of Revenue Travel Assignment Orders (RTAOs) for positions specified in E.O. 430 and Revenue Special Orders (RSOs) for all others.

3.1.2. Interim assignments shall consider the Qualification Standards (QS) and the special requirements (man specifications) of the positions. Thus, only employees who meet the QS of the positions shall be designated thereto.

3.1.3. Interim assignments shall be approved by the Commissioner upon recommendation of the following:

3.1.3.1. MANCOM — for managerial positions (down to Division Chief level)

3.1.3.2. Assistant Commissioners/ Regional Directors concerned — for non-managerial positions

3.2. Final placement actions shall take place upon approval of the Revised Staffing Pattern of the Bureau by the Department of Finance (DOF) and the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).

3.2.1. An RTAO shall be issued to confirm/finalize an employee's continued discharge of the functions which constituted his interim assignment.

3.2.2. A Screening and Selection Committee shall be constituted each for managerial and non-managerial levels to administer and implement the policies and criteria for selection and final placement of personnel as follows:

4. All personnel shall be evaluated on the basis of performance and integrity.

5. Placement of personnel shall be in accordance with the Civil Service rules and regulations.

6. Assignment/redeployment of personnel shall be dictated by the needs of the organization, however, it shall be effected with care and concern with the welfare of employees in mind.

7. An Employees Grievance Committee composed of the following shall be organized to handle attendant issues/concerns or grievances/complaints related to deployment:

C. On Staffing Pattern

1. The Bureau shall undertake a Staffing Rationalization Exercise (SRE) to determine the staffing level and position mix to support the modified structure in line with the organizational streamlining objectives.

2. The SRE shall involve the following processes:

2.1 Defining the staffing benchmarks/staffing guidelines — This shall involve the establishment of model organizational units whose manpower complement shall be used as reference figure in defining the optimum staffing configuration (number and mix) of comparable units. The management shall identify a system of classifying organizational units (e.g. Regional Offices/RDOs) and a set of criteria and weights to be used in evaluating the relative performance efficiency of organizational units.

2.2 Defining supplemental staffing guidelines — In addition to the reference staffing level defined in 2.1 above, the Deputy Commissioners and Assistant Commissioners shall review their staffing levels vis-a-vis their functions/programs and come-up with staffing proposals which shall consider the following supplemental guidelines:

2.2.1 Staffing modules for executive/management officers.

2.2.2 Flattening the organization, i.e., reduction in layers as practicable.

2.2.3 Staffing adjustments in recognition of the:

2.2.3.1 growth in taxpayer base/volume of transaction

2.2.3.2 peculiarity of the office/operations due to area coverage, topography, geographical location, accessibility, etc.

2.2.3.3 new functions/thrusts to be performed.

2.3 Preparation of staffing proposals by respective Offices/Services consistent with the supplemental staffing guidelines provided in 2.2 above for submission to MANCOM through their respective Deputy Commissioners and Assistant Commissioners.

2.4 Review and approval by MANCOM of the staffing pattern for submission to DOF and DBM.

III. REPEALING CLAUSE

All revenue issuances or portions thereof inconsistent with the provisions of this Order are hereby repealed or amended accordingly.

IV. EFFECTIVITY

This Order takes effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY-VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: All Internal Revenue Officers and Others Concerned
Original Law.To: Guidelines and Procedures on the Mass Rollout of the Integrated Tax System

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVES

This Order is issued to:

1. Ensure the "ITS-Preparedness" of the National Office (NO), Regional Offices (RO), Revenue District Offices (RDO) and Revenue Data Centers (RDC) before actual rollout date;

2. Ensure the provision of support before, during, and after the rollout;

3. Define the composition, roles, responsibilities and relationships of the various rollout support groups.

II. DEFINITION OF ROLLOUT TYPES

The ITS mass rollout shall be classified into the following types:

A. Site Rollout

The Site Rollout refers to converting a specific site to operate under ITS for the first time. The site may refer to the National Office, Revenue Data Centers, Regional Offices, or Revenue District Offices.

Rolling out an RDO for the first time shall initially involve the Registration System only, in which case the site shall be referred to as "REG-converted RDO". When the other application systems are rolled out in the REG-converted RDO, the site shall be referred to as "ITS-converted RDO".

B. Application Rollout

The Application Rollout shall refer to the implementation of the various ITS applications in a particular site. It shall be further classified into the following types:

1. Pilot Acceptance

The Pilot Acceptance refers to rolling out an application system for the first time in the pilot site(s).

2. Enhanced Application Rollout

The Enhanced Application Rollout refers to rolling out an enhanced version of the application system(s) for the first time in the pilot site(s).

3. New Application Rollout

The New Application Rollout refers to rolling out a pilot-accepted application or a user-validated enhanced application for the first time and for subsequent rollout in non-pilot site(s).

III. GUIDELINES AND PROCEDURES

A. Rollout Schedule Guidelines

The following guidelines shall be complied with in scheduling site rollout:

1. The site must be TRU-ready as reported. TRU-ready shall be defined as having 100% validated and encoded TRU records.

2. Rollout of RDOs within Metro Manila shall be prioritized over other North/South Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao RDOs.

3. Registration System shall be rolled out ahead of the other applications.

4. New applications (i.e., pilot-accepted and user-validated enhanced applications) shall be rolled out three (3) months after the application has been pilot-accepted or user-validated. New applications rollout shall not coincide with a new site rollout.

5. Enhancements shall be rolled out in phases depending on their readiness.

6. An RDC should have no more than 10% suspense rate and 10% backlog for a previously ITS-converted RDO before rolling out additional RDO(s).

7. There shall be 30-day interval between site and application rollouts.

The rollout schedule shall be presented to the Coordinating Committee meetings for approval. The Project Managers of Operations, SPIRIT, and MOST shall be responsible for informing their respective personnel of the rollout schedule for the prompt delivery of rollout requirements.

B. Rollout Tasks

Rollout tasks, classified into-pre-rollout tasks and post-rollout tasks, shall be performed and completed for every site and application rollout. The Rollout Task Matrix below shows these minor variations.

1. Pre-rollout Tasks

The pre-rollout tasks shall be completed 30-45 days prior to actual rollout. These comprise three (3) major activities:

• Pre-rollout Evaluation

• Taxpayer Record Update (TRU) Readiness Validation

• Rollout Campaign

The TRU readiness validation shall be performed simultaneously with the pre-rollout evaluation. The following are the tasks under each activity:

a) Pre-rollout Evaluation

(1) Perform tablechecking of rollout requirements using the prescribed checklists. Refer to Attachment 1 for the specific checklists and guidelines in using and accomplishing the checklists;

(2) Identify issues and action plans based on rollout requirements tablechecking;

(3) Prepare the Rollout Issue List. Refer to Attachment 2 for the Rollout Issue List template;

(4) Present issues and action plans to Coordinating Committee for review and approval;

(5) Coordinate with the different Project Managers to resolve issues and to satisfy other rollout requirements. Obtain signatures from appropriate parties to signify completion of rollout requirements.

b) TRU Readiness Validation

(1) Validate reported TRU status by conducting site visits to the certified TRU-ready RDO;

(2) Identify and resolve issues;

(3) Upload TRU records to ITS Ensure that 100% of TRU records are uploaded;

(4) Resolve suspended TRU records using as guide the TRU Suspense Resolution Procedures (Attachment 3).

c) Rollout Campaign

Rollout Campaign shall be conducted for internal and external stakeholders seven (7) days before rollout date.

(1) Organize and conduct rollout briefing/orientation sessions on rollout activities, roles and responsibilities of concerned personnel, pertinent guidelines and procedures, etc.;

(2) Prepare for official rollout launch when necessary.

2. Post-rollout Tasks

Post-rollout tasks shall be performed and completed within the first 30 days of rollout. The post-rollout activity consists mainly of implementation tasks. The Implementation Assistance Team (IAT) shall be organized to lead the implementation tasks in conjunction with the site personnel as follows:

a) Provide user support through on-the job coaching;

b) Identify and address issues/difficulties that require immediate action;

c) Identify barriers to optimum performance pertaining to technical and site environment, organization and reporting structures, policies and manual procedures, and training in order to provide long-term solution;

d) Accomplish the ITS Operations Evaluation checklists. Refer to Attachment 1 for the specific checklists and guidelines in using and accomplishing the checklists.

For pilot application rollout, the Pilot Acceptance Checklist shall be prepared and accomplished by the Project Steering Committee and Application Team assigned to the application being piloted in place of the ITS Operations Evaluation Checklist.

C. Rollout Support Groups

Key rollout support groups shall be organized to ensure the success of the rollout. These are the following:

1. Rollout Assistance Committee (RAC)

a) Composition

The RAC, which is a transitional group, is composed of BIR RDC Heads and AC-PS personnel. The RAC shall be the umbrella group in coordinating the various rollout support groups and providing overall direction pertaining to the rollout.

Refer to Attachment 4 for the Composition Chart.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

(1) Formulate a rollout strategy, criteria, guidelines and procedures to help ensure a successful rollout,

(2) Prepare a rollout schedule based on the prescribed criteria and scheduling guidelines;

(3) Ensure that the pre-rollout and post-rollout tasks are performed accordingly;

(4) Prepare RMOs, RSOs, and memos as the need arises (Example: Reminder memo for checklist accomplishment, RSO for RDC-Based Rollout Support Groups and Implementation Assistance Team, etc.);

(5) Coordinate and provide overall direction to the Information Planning Quality Standards Service-Rollout Assistance Unit (IPQS-RAU)and the RDC-based Rollout Assistance Monitors (RAM) during the transitional period.

2. Information Planning Quality Standards Service-Rollout Assistance Unit (IPQS-RAU)

a) Composition

The IPQS-RAU shall be composed of personnel from the Rollout Assistance component of the IPQS Quality Assurance Team.

Refer to Attachment 4 for the Composition Chart.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

The IPQS-RAU shall eventually take ownership of the RAC's roles and responsibilities on a long-term basis until the ITS mass rollout has been completed.

During the transitional period which shall start upon the approval of this RMO, the IPQS-RAU shall take direction from RAC. They shall work together with the RAC members in the conduct of pre-rollout and post-rollout tasks. During this period, the IPQS-RAU shall progressively assume RAC's responsibilities particularly the preparation of the pertinent RMOs, RSOs and memos.

The IPQS-RAU shall fully assume the RAC's roles and responsibilities at the end of the RAC's term of assignment.

3. RDC-Based Rollout Assistance Monitors (RDC-RAM)

a) Composition

The RDC-RAM shall be organized for each RDC. The RDC-RAM shall be manned by permanent and transitory personnel. The permanent personnel shall include the Assistant RDC Head as the Team Head and another representative from the RDC. The transitory personnel shall include one (1) representative each from all member ROs and RDOs. The RDC, RO, and RDO representatives shall preferably come from middle management positions (e.g., Section Chief, etc.) with a strong operations background.

The transitory personnel shall be identified 60 days before the rollout of the concerned RO and/or RDO within the RDC. The identified RO and/or RDO representative shall join the RDC-RAM and perform the pre-rollout and post-rollout tasks accordingly in order to prepare for the rollout of his/her respective site.

Refer to Attachment 4 for the Composition Chart.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

The RDC-RAM as a whole shall have a key role in the mass rollout of the member RDOs in their RDC area of responsibility. They shall ensure the conduct of the identified pre-rollout and post-rollout tasks for the rollout of their member RDOs. The RDC-RAM shall take overall direction and guidance from the IPQS-RAU.

4. Implementation Assistance Team (IAT)

a) Composition

Separate IATs shall be continuously organized for each site and application rollout until the completion of the ITS mass rollout. The IAT shall be made up of the IAT Management Group and the User Support Group.

Management Group

The Management Group shall be composed of the Coordinating Managers for Operations, SPIRIT and MOST, an RO Coordinator, an RDC Coordinator and an RDO Coordinator. The Coordinating Managers shall have two (2) levels-the NO-based Coordinating Managers and the Local Coordinating Managers per RDC. The NO-based Coordinating Manager positions shall be assumed by the Project Directors for Operations, SPIRIT and MOST. The Local Coordinating Manager positions shall be assumed by the Assistant Project Directors. There shall be separate and permanent sets of NO-based and Local Coordinating Managers per RDC to provide simultaneous IAT support to all the RDOs within their area of responsibility.

The Overall Local Coordinating Manager per RDC shall be selected based on his/her expertise, leadership skills and experience level. He/she shall be identified upon, preparation of the RSO.

The RO, RDC and RDO Coordinator positions shall be assumed by the RO Director or Asst. Director, the RDC Head or Assistant Head, and the RDO or Assistant RDO, respectively.

User Support Group

The User Support Group shall be composed of one (1) expert user for each application system being rolled out.

Initially, the User Support Group members for a new site shall be identified from ITS-converted sites which have the ITS expertise already. For subsequent site rollouts, the User Support Group members shall preferably come from ITS-converted sites within the same RDC.

Refer to Attachment 4 for the Composition Chart.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

The IAT shall assume direct responsibility for the conduct of the post-rollout tasks.

The specific roles and responsibilities of the IAT members are the following:

(1) NO-based Coordinating Managers-Operations, SPIRIT, MOST

The NO-based Coordinating Managers shall provide overall direction to all the IATs according to their RDC area of responsibility.

The NO-based Coordinating Managers shall provide simultaneous support to all sites being rolled out in their assigned RDC. They shall report at the sites and conduct the end-of-day debriefing for the IAT on the first week of rollout.

For simultaneous rollout of sites, they shall spend at least one (1) day per site. They shall also convene all IAT members from the rolled out sites to conduct an end-of-week debriefing.

For the second week of rollout, they shall report at the NO and conduct the end-of-week debriefing remotely through video conferencing or teleconferencing, as needed. During the debriefing, they shall address blocker or high-priority issues/problems/difficulties that are elevated by the Local Coordinating Managers.

(2) Local Coordinating Managers- Operations, SPIRIT, MOST

The Local Coordinating Managers shall provide simultaneous support to all sites being rolled out in their assigned RDC. They shall report at the sites and conduct the end-of-day debriefing on the second week of rollout in place of the NO-based Coordinating Managers.

For simultaneous rollout of sites, they shall spend at least one (1) day per site. They shall also convene all IAT members from the rolled out sites to conduct an end-of-week debriefing.

On the third week of rollout, they shall report at the NO and conduct the end-of-week debriefing remotely through video conferencing or teleconferencing, as needed. During the debriefing, they shall address blocker or high-priority issues/problems/ difficulties that are reported daily by the RDC, RO and RDO Coordinators. They shall coordinate with concerned personnel to address issues that can be immediately resolved or elevate unresolved issues to the NO-based Coordinating Managers.

(3) RO Coordinator

The RO Coordinator, being the RO representative, shall ensure that RO-related issues are addressed by the IAT and resolutions are cascaded to concerned personnel in his/her office.

He/she shall participate in the on-site and remote end-of-day and end-of-week debriefing to be conducted by the Coordinating Managers.

He/she, together with the RDC and RDO Coordinators, shall conduct the on-site end-of-day and end-of-week debriefing on the last two (2) weeks of rollout in place of the Coordinating Managers.

He/she shall also submit weekly RO status reports to the Coordinating Managers.

(4) RDC Coordinator

The RDC Coordinator, being the RDC representative, shall ensure that RDC-related issues are addressed by the IAT and resolutions are cascaded to concerned personnel in his/her office.

He/she shall participate in the on-site and remote end-of-day and end-of-week debriefing to be conducted by the Coordinating Managers.

He/she, together wish the RO and RDO Coordinators, shall conduct the on-site end-of-day and end-of-week debriefing on the last two (2) weeks of rollout in place of the Coordinating Managers.

He/she shall submit weekly RDC status reports to the Coordinating Managers.

(5) RDO Coordinator

The RDO Coordinator, being the RDO representative, shall ensure that RDO-related issues are addressed by the IAT and resolutions are cascaded to concerned personnel in his/her office.

He/she shall participate in the-on-site and remote end-of-day and end-of-week debriefing to be conducted by the Coordinating Managers.

He/she, together with the RO and RDC Coordinators, shall conduct the on-site end-of-day and end-of-week debriefing on the last two (2) weeks of rollout in place of the Coordinating Managers.

He/she shall submit weekly RDO status reports to the Coordinating Managers.

(6) User Support Group

The User Support Group members shall assist the users through on-the-job coaching in accordance with their field of expertise. Each member shall accomplish an ITS Operations Evaluation Checklist for his/her assigned application system and submit this to the Local Coordinating Managers. The User Support Group shall report to their assigned site on the first three (3) weeks of rollout and report at the designated venue for the end-of-week debriefing.

At the end of the third week they shall turn over the identified issues and action plans to the ITS Champions who shall pursue the execution of action plans and resolution of open issues.

The IAT, as a whole, shall ensure that issues and documented in accordance with existing Help Desk guidelines and procedures.

At the end of the 30-day period, the local Coordinating Managers shall present the identified issues and action plans in the Coordinating Committee meeting.

All in all, the duration of IAT involvement shall be for one (1) month. The on-site support schedule of the IAT members shall vary as shown on the table below.

5. TRU Teams

a) Composition

There shall be an NO-based TRU Team, RO-based TRU Teams and RDO-based TRU Teams.

The RO-based TRU Teams shall be headed by the Regional Directors and will have as its members three (3) representatives from the Taxpayer Assistance Service of the RO.

The RDO-based TRU Teams shall be composed of the Data Capture, Data Validation, and Data Encoding Teams whose members are RDO personnel as specified in RMO 35-96.

Refer to Attachment 4 for the Composition Chart.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

(1) NO-based TRU Team

The NO-based TRU Team shall provide the overall direction to the RO TRU Teams. They shall conduct briefings to explain the site visit guidelines and procedures to be accomplished by the RO TRU Teams. They shall also be responsible for consolidating the TRU status reports from the RDOs and furnishing copies of the consolidated report to the RO TRU Teams and the RAC/IPQS-RAU.

(2) RO-based TRU Team Head

The RO-based TRU Team Head shall manage the overall TRU activities of the Regional TRU Team. He/she shall:

• Monitor the TRU activities of the member RDOs and ensure that the procedures specified in RMO 35-96 and Attachment 5 of this RMO are being accomplished;

• Report any non-compliance to TRU policies, procedures and guidelines and other TRU-related problems found in the member RDOs to the NO TRU Team for their action; and

• Conduct status meetings with the Revenue District Officers to facilitate issue resolutions and completion of TRU, as needed.

He/she shall be the central repository of TRU information in the RO. The TRU information may come in the form of TRU status reports and Site Visit Reports prepared by the RDO-based and RO-based TRU Team members, respectively.

(3) RO-based TRU Team Members

The RO-based TRU Team members shall:

• Conduct site visits to RDOs with the following objectives:

— ensure proper compliance to TRU policies and procedures as stated in RMO 35-96 and Attachment 5 of this RMO;

— issue Certificate of TRU Readiness (Attachment 7) for RDOs with 100% validated and encoded records 45 days before the scheduled rollout;

— assist RDOs in resolving suspended TRU records;

— monitor and ensure 100% uploading of TRU records to ITS.

• Raise issues that cannot be resolved at the RO/RDO level to the RDC TRU Head; and

• Prepare Site Visit Reports.

(4) RDO-based TRU Team

The RDO-based TRU team shall ensure an accurate and complete implementation of TRU Phase I according to the guidelines and procedures specified in RMO 35-96 and Attachment 5 of this RMO.

The RO-based and RDO-based TRU Teams shall work closely with the designated RAC/IPQS-RAU/RDC-RAT representative(s) who shall conduct site visits prior to the rollout, assist in the uploading of TRU records to ITS, and identify issues and action plans as necessary.

6. Change Management Team

a) Composition

There shall be an NO-based Change Management Team composed of a Team Head and at least four (4) members preferably with ITS background. Each member shall have an assigned RDC.

Refer to Attachment 4 for the Composition Chart.

b) Roles and-Responsibilities

The Change Management Team shall be responsible for the organization, preparation and conduct of the rollout campaign as part of the pre-rollout tasks. Specifically, they shall perform the following tasks:

• Schedule and organize the orientation/briefing sessions on rollout activities, roles and responsibilities of concerned personnel, pertinent guidelines and procedures, etc.;

• Coordinate with the orientation/briefing session speakers and participants;

• Prepare the necessary orientation/briefing materials;

• Conduct presentations when necessary.

7. Site Heads

a) Composition

The Site Heads pertains to the different heads of office in the Bureau. These are the RDC Heads, RO Directors, and RDO Heads.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

The Site Heads shall take full ownership of ensuring the success of rollout in his/her respective site by coordinating with the appropriate personnel to meet the rollout requirements. He/she shall report the pre-rollout and post-rollout status of his site in the Coordinating Committee meetings.

8. ITS Champions

a) Composition

The ITS Champions identified by the Site Heads shall be composed of one (1) expert user per system. However, an expert user may have expertise on more than one (1) application system.

The ITS Champions shall undergo ITS training and on-the-job training.

The following list shall initially be used as guide in identifying the ITS Champions:

b) Roles and Responsibilities

The ITS Champions shall be responsible for pursuing the resolution of open issues and execution of action plans turned over by the IAT at the end of their assignment. The ITS Champions shall provide status of the issues to the Site Heads who shall then report it in the Coordinating Committee meetings.

9. Help Desk (NO/RDC/RDO)

a) Composition

There will be Help Desk personnel at the RDO, RO, RDC, and NO level. The specific composition of the Help Desk Teams is defined in the Help Desk Primer.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

The Help Desk is a single, central point of end-user contact for all types of problems, whether technical or non-technical (procedure and resource problems) as well as ITS or non-ITS problems. Generally, the Help Desk teams are responsible for the following:

• Receipt and logging of problems/issues raised by end users and the IAT from the sites;

• Provision of appropriate support through the resolution of issues;

• Elevation of problems to succeeding levels of support, if necessary;

• Informing end users of problem status, whether resolved or open;

• Updating of the problem log.

10. Application Systems Support and Maintenance (ASM) Team

a) Composition

The ASM Team shall be composed of the NO-based ASM personnel, two (2) on-site ASM Team Leads and on-site Enhancement Support. The on-site Enhancement Support shall be provided only during enhanced application rollout and shall have the expertise on the enhanced application(s).

Refer to Attachment 4 for the Composition Chart.

b) Roles and Responsibilities

(1) NO-based ASM personnel

The NO-based ASM personnel shall be responsible for the resolution of all application-related issues/problems, whether functional or technical in nature. They shall implement the fixes/solutions and enhancements on the applications. They shall also communicate all application changes/enhancements to the concerned personnel. They shall ensure that the necessary ASM personnel are provided on-site.

(2) ASM Team Lead

The ASM Team Lead shall report at the site for the first two (2) weeks of rollout and when transaction volume is expected to increase during the rollout. He/she shall provide immediate general support for the applications through on-the-job coaching, addressing questions/issues, troubleshooting and recommending workground/interim procedures.

(3) Enhancement Support

The Enhancement Support shall report at the site for the first two (2) weeks of rollout. He/she shall provide immediate enhanced application-specific support through on-the-job coaching, addressing questions/issues, troubleshooting and recommending workground/interim procedures.

Pilot Acceptance Framework

January 14, 1997

Re: Pilot Acceptance Framework

This memorandum with attachments documents the agreement reached between the BIR and AC-PS regarding the pilot Sign-off Framework.

Conforme: Conforme:

(Sgd.) Carol E. Carreon (Sgd.) David P. Nilsen

BIR-Deputy Commissioner AC-PS Deputy Project Director

Re: PILOT SIGN-OFF FRAMEWORK

1. Introduction:

The purpose of this memorandum is to define the framework, acceptance criteria and sign-off responsibility for the Pilot project, which is identified in the IFB, the Special Conditions of Contract, the Inception Report and the Billing Model.

This memorandum covers the Pilot for the Systems provided in Attachment D. The Pilot will be conducted at the Manila RDC and the NO.

The pilot contains two parts — Pilot Test and Pilot Operations. The Pilot Test is run by AC-PS. The Pilot Operations are conducted by the Bureau. These are the only differences between the two parts of the Pilot; all other roles, procedures, and working arrangements are as provided in Section 4.

The Pilot Test and Pilot Operations periods are defined in Attachment E.

2. Acceptance Criteria

The criteria for acceptance of the Pilot are:

a. Tax Application Processing

The conditions defined in Attachment A for a given application are satisfied as per functional specification. These conditions will be progressively verified, and will include conditions relating to conversion (where appropriate)

b. Stress and Performance Tests

Stress and Performance Tests will be satisfied as specified in Attachment B.

c. Documentation

The documentation that the BIR and AC-PS have previously agreed will be maintained is up-to-date. The list of the agreed maintainable documentation is provided in Attachment C.

d. Major SIRs (Production or Pre-Production) will be resolved prior to acceptance of the application or item that is the subject of the error.

• Functionality issues will be resolved separately. The target timeframe for preparation of a workplan for open functionality issues, is the end of Pilot.

• Results of the Stress and Performance Tests will be a component of the Equipment Acceptance.

3. Acceptance Timeframe

Acceptance activities of the Bureau will occur during the Pilot. Acceptance activities, including error and point logging, will not extend beyond the end of the Pilot.

Application systems will be evaluated progressively against the acceptance criteria in 2.a. When the criteria in 2.a and 2.d have been satisfied for a given application, that application will be accepted.

Acceptance of the last application covered by this framework will be conditional on the prior acceptance of the deliverables identified in 2.b and 2.c and the resolution of major SIRs (2.d) not identifiable with an application.

4. Working Arrangements, Procedures and Guidelines

To ensure that acceptance is conducted in a consistent, timely and efficient manner, BIR and AC-PS agree to the following working arrangements, procedures and guidelines. These apply on a per application basis, and equally during Pilot Test and Pilot Operation.

Production SIRs

1. The Pilot users will log all production issues with the Help Desk.

2. The Help Desk log must include the name of the person raising the issue, and where the originator is not a PAT User, the Help Desk must assign the issue to the most appropriate PAT User.

3. The Help Desk will provide AC-PS with a copy of the Production Issue Log on a daily basis such that AC-PS is notified within 24 hours (i.e. next business day) of the BIR recognizing the production issue.

4. AC-PS will analyze the issue raised, and either assign a SIR if an error, or indicate that an enhancement is required, or respond directly with a comment/explanation of the non-system action(s) to be taken, and update the Help Desk accordingly. Enhancements will be dealt with separately.

5. Where an error SIR has been raised AC-PS will fix, test and migrate (to Staging) the necessary programs.

6. The ASM team will conduct tests in Staging to confirm that the error SIR has been implemented correctly, and inform AC-PS accordingly.

7. ASM will notify the BIR ISOS staff via a Migration Request that the corrected programs are in Staging ready for migration to Production.

8. The BIR ISOS staff will migrate the programs from Staging to Production as requested (on a twice weekly basis).

9. AC-PS will notify the Help Desk that the error SIR — cross referenced to the appropriate issue (log) — has been actioned and that the fix is in Production.

10. The Help Desk will advise the assigned PAT user that the issue has been rectified ready for his/her confirmation in Pilot.

11. The assigned PAT user will then confirm via testing that the issue has been corrected, and will inform the Help Desk of the success or otherwise.

12. The Help Desk upon notification by the PAT User will update the Production Issues Log by changing the SIR status to Closed, or by notifying AC-PS that the SIR remains Open.

13. If the SIR remains Open, steps 3-12 are repeated until the SIR is Closed.

At Pilot End

14. The Help Desk will provide a list of all Production Issues/SIRs to the Project Director and AC-PS as at the end of the Pilot period.

15. AC-PS will consolidate these issues with the Pilot Acceptance Issues Log and provide a copy of the consolidated list to the Project Director.

16. No further production issues will be added to the Pilot Acceptance Issues Log, beyond the last day of the Pilot, except where:

16.1. The implementation of a SIR creates further errors, or

16.2. A Blocker error prevents conduct of the Pilot, in which case a period of fifteen (15) calendar days from the date of the Blocker fix being migrated to Production will be provided.

17. AC-PS will drive steps 3-12 to resolve all items within the consolidated Pilot Acceptance Issues Log.

18. The Project Director will be updated periodically as the SIRs are closed following testing/confirmation by the assigned PAT user(s).

Pilot Acceptance/Rejection

19. The designated parties responsible for advising on functional and/or technical acceptance will complete and provide to the Project Director a signed Product Acceptance/Rejection Advice Notice when all major SIRs relating to an application are closed.

20. The designees should only use the correct Product Acceptance Advise forms. Any points to which the sign-of is conditional should be provided in summary form on a Condition List that is to be attached to the Product Acceptance Advice Notice. The Condition List should be cross-referenced to the Pilot Acceptance Issues Log where further detailed comments/information relating to each condition will be provided.

21. The Project Director will inform AC-PS of the Pilot acceptance or otherwise via a Product Acceptance/Rejection Certificate upon receipt of Product Acceptance/Rejection Advice Notices from all assigned designees for the Pilot Acceptance of that application (and subject to the other acceptance criteria specified in Sections 2 and 3, being satisfied).

22. By application, if no major outstanding points exist then acceptance must be provided.

23. The following cannot hold up acceptance and payment of the Pilot:

23.1. BIR failure to create a transaction to demonstrate RDC communication within the timeframe.

23.2. Data errors not caused by the ITS, excluding failure of the ITS to validate as per functional specifications.

23.3. Business transactions that do not naturally occur within the timeframe of the Pilot.

23.4. Operational errors not due to the ITS.

23.5. Transactions correctly identified by the system as exception transactions.

23.6. Willful and/or malicious misuse, non-use or dislike of the system by end users.

23.7. Low volume of transactions processed by ITS due to:

• low number of registered taxpayers

• level of BIR resources and the skills of these resources

• the BIR organization and its procedures and other such non-ITS related reasons.

23.8. Non-compliance by external parties with mutually agreed ITS procedures. External parties include affiliated banks and collection agencies, the Bureau of Treasury, other government entities.

23.9. Errors of a minor nature.

23.10. Errors caused as a result of enhancement or maintenance work.

24. After AC-PS has reported that an error is fixed, the BIR has two (2) work days from the natural occurrence of that transaction to disagree provided that it occurs during the Pilot Operations. Where the natural occurrence of the transaction occurs after the end of the Pilot the transaction shall be tested by the PAT users (with the assistance of ASM) in Staging.

25. Any enhancements to the tax application software and associated architecture, including documentation, performed after the start of the Pilot will not be subject to Pilot Acceptance.

Pre-Production SIRs

26. Prior to Pilot the Expert Users should test the major Pre-Production SIRs as they are resolved by AC-PS, update the Discrepancy Log and SIR Log, and notify AC-PS accordingly (in particular if the issue/SIR remains Open).

27. AC-PS will provide to the Project Director a list of all Pre-Production SIRs as at the first day of the Pilot.

28. AC-PS will during Pilot, and as the outstanding major Pre-Production SIRs are resolved, inform ASM that these SIRs are ready for re-test in Staging.

29. ASM will test and update the Pre-Production SIR Log, and notify AC-PS accordingly (in particular if the SIR remains Open).

30. AC-PS will maintain independently one consolidated issues log that comprises both Pre-Production and Production SIRs.

Line Management Reporting

31. To monitor progress, and ensure that acceptance objectives are achieved, Pilot status will be reported by BIR at Project Line Management and MAC meetings.

32. During the Project Line Management meetings the number of verified conditions, unverified conditions and conditions failing verification will be reported.

33. Disagreements of any nature relating to Pilot Acceptance will be resolved via the arbitration process, and discussion at the weekly Project Line Management meeting.

5. Sign-Off Responsibility

• The CIR, or designee, has sign-off responsibility for each application system.

Original Law.Subject: All Enhancement Project Managers, BIR Project Management Office (BIR - PMO), and Other Internal Revenue Officers and Employees Concerned
Original Law.To: Policies and Procedures on the Validation of Enhancement Deliverables under the BIR Tax Computerization Project (TCP) and the Designation of Signatories of Enhancement Documents

Details.Details:
I. Objectives/Scope:

In line with the BIR-Philippine Tax Computerization Project (PTCP), popularly known as Systems for Philippine Internal Revenue Information Technology (SPIRIT), this Revenue Memorandum Order is issued to achieve the following objectives:

(a). to ensure that enhancement deliverables are validated uniformly across the BIR;

(b). to ensure that enhancement deliverables conform to an acceptable standard and meet the Bureau's requirements and relevant User Validation Criteria;

(c). to provide policy guidelines and procedures in processing all pending and future enhancement deliverables;

(d). to designate revenue officials and personnel to validate enhancement deliverables and sign User Validation documents.

II. Roles and Responsibilities:

A. Project Manager

1. The Project Manager has primary management and staffing responsibility for the conduct of the Quality Test.

2. The Project Manager is responsible for monitoring the overall status of the deliverable and ensuring that all issues raised are properly addressed.

3. The Project Manager, together with the Expert User, shall notify the Receiving User when an enhancement is ready for review.

4. In connection with No. 3, the Project Manager shall prepare the User Validation Certificate and transmit it together with all supporting documents (Acceptance Checklist, conditions list, letters, memos, etc.) to the Receiving User.

B. Enhancement Team

(Project Manager, ISG, Expert User)

1. The Enhancement Team shall perform Quality Testing on the enhancement deliverable.

2. The Enhancement Team shall gather/log all issues/conditions pertaining to the enhancement under review.

3. The Enhancement Team shall resolve issues/conditions raised on the deliverable.

4. The Enhancement Team shall provide the Receiving User the environment required to re-execute tests.

5. If so requested, the Enhancement Team shall assist the Receiving User in the performance of User Validation tests.

III. Guidelines and Procedures:

A. Policy/Guidelines for Validation of Enhancements:

1. All enhancements to the Integrated Tax System (ITS) that

a. involve a change in functionality,

b. have an impact on other applications,

c. materially change the user interface, or

d. add a new module

require a completely signed User Validation Certificate before migration to production.

2. The Bureau can use enhancements in production only when there are no outstanding major issues or when remaining outstanding issues are minor. Nevertheless, the Bureau strongly discourages the use in production of enhancements with outstanding issues, regardless of severity. The Enhancement Team is enjoined to exert all necessary efforts to resolve all issues before issuance of a User Validation Certificate.

3. Procedures for User Validation, including the classification of issues into Major/Minor are prescribed in Attachment A, "User Validation Procedure."

4. A completely signed User Validation Certificate allows for migration of an enhancement to production.

B. The following documents are attached for the guidance of all concerned:

1. Acceptance Checklist (Annex A)

2. List of all Issues/Conditions raised on the deliverable (Annex B)

3. Classification of Issues by Severity (Major/Minor) (Annex C)

4. User Validation Certificate for enhancement deliverables with no outstanding conditions (Annex D)

C. Expert User

In addition to the functions the Expert User will perform as a member of the Enhancement Team,

1. The Expert User shall initial each page of the Acceptance Checklist once all items are fulfilled.

2. The Expert User, together with the Project Manager, shall notify the Receiving User when an enhancement is ready for review.

D. Receiving User

1. The Receiving User shall determine whether the enhancement developed by the Enhancement Team satisfied the Bureau's requirements, performing hands-on tests as deemed necessary.

2. The Receiving User shall inform the Project Manager of additional issues that require resolution.

3. The Receiving User is responsible for the issuance of a completely signed User Validation Certificate, providing one set of the User Validation documents to the following:

— Project Manager of the relevant enhancement (original copy)

— Project Director

— Project Management Office (PMO)

4. The Receiving User shall keep one set of the User Validation documents on file.

E. Project Management Office (PMO)

1. The Project Management Office shall keep on file User Validation documents received from the receiving User.

5. [n] User Validation Certificate for enhancement deliverables with outstanding minor conditions (Annex E)

6. User Validation Procedure Flowchart (Annex F)

This Order takes effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: Guidelines and Procedures on the Handling of Out-of-District/Out-of-System Tax Returns/Payment Forms Received in Computerized and Non-Computerized Revenue District Offices (RDOs)
Original Law.To: All Regional Directors, Revenue District Officers, Heads of Revenue Data Centers and Revenue Officers and All Others Concerned

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVES

This Order is issued to:

1. Prescribe the procedures and guidelines in the proper disposition of Out-of-District/Out-of-System Tax Returns/Payment Forms.

2. Delineate the functions of each of office/division/unit in the handling of Out-of-District/Out-of-System Tax Returns/ Payment Forms.

II. DEFINITION OF TERMS

1. Out-of-District (OOD) tax returns/payment forms — Tax returns or payment forms received by an Authorized Agent Bank in an RDO other than the Home RDO of the Taxpayer. Specifically, this refers to:

Case 1 — OOD tax returns/payment forms belonging to a computerized RDO but received by a non-computerized RDO.

Case 2 — OOD tax returns/payment forms belonging to a non-computerized RDO but received by a computerized RDO.

2. Out-of-System (OOS) tax return payment forms — Tax returns or payment forms received by a computerized RDO but belonging to another computerized RDO under a different Revenue Data Center.

3. Payment Form — Form used by taxpayers to pay a tax liability not covered by a particular tax return.

4. Home RDO — refers to the Revenue District Office having jurisdiction over the taxpayer's domicile or legal residence, principal office or place of business, where the taxpayer is required to register under the TRU program.

5. Computerized RDO — An RDO where the Integrated Tax System or part of it is already in place.

6. Non-Computerized RDO — An RDO where not one of the ITS application systems has been installed.

III. PROCEDURES

The following procedures shall be enforced by the RDOs, Revenue Data Centers (RDCs) and Information Systems Operations Service (ISOS) in handling Out-of-District/Out-of-System Tax Returns/Payment Forms.

1. For Case #1 — OOD Tax Returns/Payment Forms belonging to a Computerized RDO but received by a Non-Computerized RDO

A. Non-Computerized RDO

1. Segregate the Out-of-District Tax Returns/Payment Forms from the NPCS batches of returns/payment forms retrieved from the AABs;

2. Photocopy the Out-of-District tax returns/ payment forms and return the originals to the NPCS batches;

3. Batch the photocopies of the Out-of-District tax returns/payment forms received during the week. Prepare manually a BCS using the prescribed format;

4. Prepare a transmittal list for Out-of-District tax returns/payment forms received during the week indicating therein the bank branch code and the BCS number of the batch where the tax returns were taken;

5. Transmit the BCS together with the photocopies of the out-of-district tax returns/payment forms to the RDC concerned not later than three (3) days after the receipt of the documents for encoding of payment details; and

6. Furnish ISOS with copies of the transmittal list, BCS and returns/payment forms for updating of the NPCS Masterfile.

B. Revenue Data Center (RDC)

1. Encode data of out-of-district tax returns/payment forms received from the Non-Computerized RDOs using the Bank Data Entry program;

2. Use the Bank DE program to download the data to diskette, or to a shared drive;

3. Perform Data Diskette Processing;

4. After uploading is completed, perform processing using the existing Bank Data Entry procedures; and

5. Process the data according to existing ITS procedures.

C. Information Systems Operations Service (ISOS)

1. Encode data needed for updating NPCS files pertaining to the Out-of-district tax returns/payment forms received;

2. Update Masterfile of NPCS records of the Home RDO by including data from OOD returns/payment forms. Likewise, records of source RDO must be corrected by deleting previous data captured from the same OOD documents; and

3. File transmittal list of Out-of-District tax returns/payment forms.

2. For Case #2 — OOD Tax Returns/Payment Forms belonging to a Non-computerized RDO but received by a Computerized RDO.

A. Revenue Data Center (RDC)

1. Identify Out-of-District Tax Returns/Payment Forms through the Payment Suspense Worksheet where the correct RDO of the TP is identified through payment;

2. Use the appropriate function key: CTRLT (cf.SUG) to show the Payment Modify Screen wherein the suspended taxpayer transaction is flagged as OOD. Send to ISOS these OOD files via electronic transfer.

3. Segregate the out-of-district tax returns of taxpayers belonging to the computerized RDO from the CBR batches;

4. Encode data from the tax returns/payment forms;

5. Photocopy the out-of-district tax returns/payment forms;

6. Return the originals to the CBR batches;

7. Batch the photocopied tax returns/payment forms as follows:

7.1 Segregate the batching from old forms from the new forms;

7.2 Segregate the batching per the Home RDO code of the taxpayer;

7.3 Batch the tax returns/payment forms in 50's at the most; and

7.4 Manually prepare a Batch Control Sheet (BCS) A or B per batch with a BCS number as per the standard (e.g., 90001) with the Home RDO indicated by the receiving bank.

8. Send the batched out-of-district tax returns/payment forms to Home RDO.

B. Non-Computerized RDO

1. Receive batches of out-of-district returns from Revenue Data Center; and

2. Process returns in accordance with RMO No. 29-91 which Prescribes the Procedures on the Receipt, Transmittal and Processing of Tax Returns Filed Thru the Banks under the New Payment Control System (NPCS).

C. Information System Operations Service (ISOS)

1. Based on files sent by RDC via electronic transfer, extract out-of-district files from ITS database;

2. Merge files with NPCS files from pertinent non-computerized Home RDOs; and

3. Generate corrected NPCS filers reports.

3. For Case #3 — Out-of-System Tax Returns/Payment Forms

A. Source RDC shall:

1. Forward Out-of-System (OOS) tax returns/payment forms to appropriate RDC having jurisdiction over them.

2. Send data captured by source RDC to appropriate RDC via electronic transfer.

B. Appropriate RDC shall pro cess data from OOS tax returns/payment forms in accordance with prescribed ITS procedures.

IV. EFFECTIVITY

This Order shall take effect immediately upon approval.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: Pilot Implementation of a Technical Procedures Unit in the Collection Division, Revenue Region No. 12, Bacolod City
Original Law.To: All Internal Revenue Officials and Employees of Revenue Region No. 12, Bacolod City

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVES:

This Order is being issued for the following purposes:

1. To create a Technical Procedures Unit for pilot testing in Revenue Region No. 12, Bacolod City; and

2. To specify the policies and guidelines governing the operations of the Unit.

II. POLICIES AND GUIDELINES:

The following policies and guidelines shall be observed in the creation and administration of the Technical Procedures (TP) Unit:

1. The TP Unit shall be attached to the Collection Division of Revenue Region No. 12, Bacolod City.

2. Initially, the TP Unit shall be staffed by one (1) revenue official, who shall act as both TP Unit Chief and Technical Procedures Advisor.

The TP Unit staff shall be augmented once the volume of work at the Unit has reached sufficient levels to warrant the assignment of additional personnel.

3. The TP Advisors shall provide assistance and technical advice to the Revenue Collection Officers of the various Revenue Districts of Revenue Region No. 12, relative to the following collection functions:

3.1 Seizure and sale of real or personal property;

3.2 Sale and disposal of forfeited and acquired assets;

3.3 Review and evaluation of compromise settlements;

3.4 Creation and maintenance of the Regional Tax Lien Data Base; and

3.5 Identification of non-filers for one-time tax liabilities.

4. Chapter IX of the BIR Collection Manual (Annex A hereof) shall specify the duties and responsibilities of the Technical Procedures Advisors.

5. The Chief of the TP Unit shall report to the Collection Division Chief on the progress of the Unit's pilot operations.

6. The Collection Division Chief shall exercise direct supervision over the TP Unit Chief, and shall report to the Assistant Commissioner (Collection), through the Revenue Regional Director, on all developments in the pilot operations of the Unit.

The Revenue Regional Director shall, in turn, have full control over the TP Unit Pilot Project.

7. The pilot test operations shall be evaluated until August 30, 1997, to determine appropriate adjustments, if any, that must be made to the Project, and to assess the feasibility of establishing similar TP Units at other Regional Offices.

III. REPEALING CLAUSE

This Order shall NOT amend or repeal any Revenue Memorandum Order, Revenue Administrative Order, or any promulgation of similar nature, concerning the performance of the Bureau's collection function.

IV. EFFECTIVITY

This Order shall take effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: Prescribing Revised Procedures in Requesting Information from Tax Treaty Partners Pursuant to the Philippine Tax Treaties
Original Law.To: All Internal Revenue Officers Concerned

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVES:

At present, the Philippines has twenty-four (24) effective tax treaties with other countries. These treaties provide for exchange of information procedures, wherein the competent authority of each treaty country can request for information from his counterpart for the purpose of assessment, collection, enforcement and/or prosecution of income tax cases.

This Order is therefore issued to:

1. Keep the Bureau abreast of developments occurring in other countries which are relevant to the administration of our tax laws.

2. Prescribe standard procedures in requesting information from tax treaty partners.

II. POLICIES:

To achieve the above objectives, the following policies are hereby prescribed:

A. The information which may be requested shall include but is not limited to the following:

1. Any information necessary for the proper determination/assessment of the income tax of taxpayers such as:

a. Name of a particular Filipino citizen, his investments, real property interest and income in that country;

b. Confirmation of whether or not a particular person claiming for a tax treaty benefit is in fact a resident of that country;

c. The true beneficial owner of a dividend, interest, or royalty held by a nominee or trustee;

d. Information needed for the proper allocation of taxable profits and expenses between a related company in that country and in the Philippines. This refers to transfer pricing, i.e., the nature and amount of expenses, prices and charges by a head office, parent company or any other controlling or controlled corporation which are charged, wholly or partially, to its branch, subsidiary, or controlled corporation in the Philippines. The transaction may cover sale of tangible goods, interest or loans, royalties, payment for services rendered and others;

e. Income of public entertainers paid by a resident of a treaty-country for services rendered in the Philippines.

2. Any information which will help in the administration of our Income Tax Laws even if it does not concern the application of any particular provision in the convention between the Philippines and with our tax treaty partners, such as laws, administrative rulings, court decisions, official publications and others.

B. The above information may be requested from any of the following countries:

C. All request for information from tax treaty partners shall be coursed through International Tax Affairs Division (ITAD) prior to approval of the Commissioner.

D. Under no circumstances shall a revenue official communicate directly to the competent authority and/or representative of a treaty country on matters to these requests for information.

III. PROCEDURES:

A. Requesting Party

1. Accomplish BIR Form TC-003 (form attached) to request for information with a treaty counterpart country;

2. Forward duly accomplished TC-003 to immediate superior approval;

3. Forward approved BIR Form TC-003 to ITAD for processing.

B. ITAD

1. Receive duly approved TC-003 from requesting party;

2. Prepare necessary communication/memo-request for information to the concerned authority of the treaty counterpart country;

3. Forward communication/memo-request to the Office of the Commissioner thru channels, for review and signature;

4. Receive from the office of the Commissioner signed communication/memo-request and forward the same to the treaty counterpart country thru the General Services Division;

5. Receive and forward to requesting party response/reply on the request made.

IV. REPEALING CLAUSE:

This Order amends RMO Nos. 4-83 and 50-89 and all other issuances or portion thereof inconsistent herewith.

V. EFFECTIVITY:

This Order takes effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: Prescribing the Use of the Operations Manual for the Integrated Tax System (ITS)
Original Law.To: All Internal Revenue Officers Concerned

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVES

This Order is issued to:

1. Document the streamlined processes, policies, guidelines and procedures developed under the Integrated Tax System (ITS);

2. Ensure uniformity and consistency of actions to be taken in the discharge of official functions as defined under the ITS; and

3. Prescribe officially the usage of the Operations Manual which integrates the Common User Guide, System User Guide and the Manual Procedures Guide.

II. SCOPE AND COVERAGE

The use of the Operations Manual (OM) by all Revenue personnel concerned in the ITS pilot and/or roll-out sites shall be mandatory and will initially cover the following application systems:

1. Registration System (REG)

2. Returns Processing System (RPS)

3. Collection and Bank Reconciliation System (CBR)

4. Case Monitoring System (CMS)

5. Taxpayer Accounting System (TAS)

6. Returns Compliance System (RCS)

7. Accounts Receivable System (ARS)

8. Audit System (AUD)

9. Tax Credit/Refund System (TCRS)

The processes for the other ITS application systems will be incorporated in the OM as they become available. A separate RMO shall prescribe the usage of such processes.

III. GUIDELINES AND PROCEDURES

1. The OM is a consolidation of the System User Guide, Manual Procedures Guide and Common User Guide prepared for the various ITS applications. Henceforth, it shall be the only official reference on matters involving computerized and manual processes, policies, guidelines and procedures relative to the discharge of the Bureau's functions as defined under the ITS.

2. The Operations Manual Project shall be responsible for the maintenance of the OM until such time that a unit or division has been created for the purpose. Such unit or division shall be created not later than the roll-out date of the last ITS application. Pending such creation, all policy and procedural changes in the system, whether technical or manual, which affect the OM shall be communicated by all concerned offices within the Bureau to the Manager of the Operations Manual Project for the corresponding modification or revision of the OM.

3. For purposes of this Order, Version 1.2 of the OM shall be the final OM. This may be modified or revised whenever necessary. However, implementation of a modified or revised version of the OM shall require the issuance of a Revenue Memorandum Circular informing all concerned of the updates.

IV. REPEALING CLAUSE

The provisions of any Revenue Memorandum Order, Revenue Memorandum Circular or any other revenue issuance inconsistent with the Operations Manual are hereby repealed, amended or revoked accordingly.

V. EFFECTIVITY

This Order takes effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: All Chiefs of Offices/Divisions Units, Systems Administrators, Computer Operators and others concerned
Original Law.To: Policies and Guidelines on Office Automation Security in the National Office (N.O.) and the Revenue Data Center (RDC)

Details.Details:
I. Objectives:

This Order is for the purpose of providing policies and guidelines on the following:

• To promote awareness among users about virus prevention and control.

• To prevent proliferation of computer viruses and safeguard the data integrity of the Bureau's office automation systems and files.

• To maintain a virus-free computer environment.

II. Policies and Guidelines

In order to attain these objectives, the following are to be observed:

A. All disk drives of Office Automation PCs connected to the network shall be disabled except for one (1) dedicated PC which shall serve as the entry point in uploading and downloading of files in every division/office.

B. The dedicated PC with anti-virus software shall be installed in a prominent location which users can easily access. This shall be manned by a designated Computer Operator who shall be responsible for its operation and maintenance.

C. All diskettes/cartridges/tapes shall be scanned for viruses through the dedicated PC prior to loading.

D. In order to ensure data integrity and to avoid loss of files due to viruses, periodic back-up shall be created.

E. Use of unlicensed software is strongly discouraged. Likewise, copying and installation of game software are not allowed.

F. Penalties/Sanctions shall be imposed on violators of the above-stated policies and shall be dealt with accordingly, upon recommendation of the Assistant Commissioner, Information Systems Operations Service (ISOS) for the National Office or Revenue Data Center (RDC) Head for the RDC and attached Regional Offices/Revenue District Office to the RDC.

• First Offense: Verbal admonition and a written reprimand will be issued and shall form part of his/her 201 files.

• Second Offense: All the PCs in the concerned office will be temporarily disconnected from the network and will only be re-connected until after such time that the violator has been evaluated to be abiding by the said set of policies.

• Third Offense: The Internal Security Office will be notified of the violator's non-compliance to this Order for the necessary administrative action in accordance with the Civil Service rules.

G. Detailed technical procedures for implementation will be provided in a separate Memorandum.

III. Effectivity

This Order takes effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: Prescribing the Policies and Procedures in the Implementation of Operation "Even Returns"
Original Law.To: All Revenue District Officers and Others Concerned

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVES:

This Office has noted that a number of withholding agents have been remiss in their application of the Withholding Tax Table, as evidenced by the number of compensation income earners paying additional income taxes on April 15 and July 15.

In support of the Withholding Tax Program for 1997 embodied in Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 2-97 as a BIR Priority Program, all Revenue District Officers shall implement Operation "Even Returns", a special activity of the Operations Group, which is designed to:

1. Raise the level of voluntary compliance of Withholding Agents;

2. Increase the level of awareness of Withholding Agents on rules and regulations concerning the correct withholding and timely remittance of taxes withheld; and

3. Encourage employers to periodically verify and update the information furnished by their employees, as a prerequisite to proper withholding of taxes.

II. POLICIES AND GUIDELINES

In the implementation of Operation "Even Returns", all Revenue District Officers shall be guided by the following:

1. All Revenue District Officers shall check the levels of compliance of all Withholding Agents in their jurisdiction, by segregating all taxable returns filed by employees earning compensation income from only one (1) employer.

2. The appropriate penalties shall be strictly enforced for non-withholding and/or under-remittance of withholding taxes.

III. PROCEDURE

The following procedures shall be observed in Operation "Even Returns":

1. Gather all taxable 1996 returns filed by taxpayers earning compensation income from only one (1) employer.

The following returns shall NOT be included:

a. Those filed by employees earning compensation income from more than one (1) employer;

b. Those filed by employees whose employers are not registered with the Revenue District Office concerned; and

c. Those filed without a copy of the taxpayer's Certificate of Income Tax Withheld on Compensation (Form No. W-2).

2. Group these returns according to the taxpayers' employer, and assign them to a Revenue Officer (Assessment) through a Revenue Verification Order (RVO).

3. Summarize the pertinent data contained in the returns, in accordance with the format for the List of Taxable Returns (Form 1701-A) of Compensation Income Earners prescribed in Annex A.

4. Compute the difference between the total tax due and total tax withheld for all employees of a particular employer who filed taxable returns. The total difference shall serve as the basis for the computation of surcharges and interests that must be paid by the Withholding Agent (Employer) concerned. The following formula may be used in computing the total surcharge and interest due:

Basic Tax Due (Based on the attached List of Employees)

========

25% Surcharge (Basic Tax x 0.25)

20% Interest* (Basic Tax + Surcharge)

Compromise Penalty

-------------

TOTAL SURCHARGES AND INTEREST DUE

========

* Interest should run from the date the tax should have been remitted to April 15 of the following year. For uniformity in the application of interest for returns filed for taxable year 1996, interest may be computed from January 25 to April 15, 1997.

5. Inform the Withholding Agent (Employer) concerned of the total surcharges and interest payable, and compromise penalties. Formats for the official communications to both government Agencies/Instrumentalities and Withholding Agents from the private sector, informing them of the assessed penalties, are attached as Annexes B and C of this Order.

For this purpose, penalties shall be imposed on:

a. For Government Withholding Agents — the Chief Accountant, Head of Accounting, or Financial Officer of the Agency/Office (Annex B); or

b. For Private Withholding Agents — the registered individual owner, corporation, or partnership (Annex C).

6. In the event that the Withholding Agent fails to respond to the written notice of penalties incurred within fifteen (15) days from receipt of said notice, the Revenue Officer concerned shall immediately report the assessment as an audit case, following standard audit reporting procedures and requirements.

7. The Head of the Assessment Unit in each Revenue District Office, shall supervise the implementation of this Order, and shall report to the Revenue District Officer concerned any developments therein.

8. This activity must be concluded not later than Friday, August 29, 1997.

IV. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

All Revenue District Officers must submit to the Office of the Assistant Commissioner (Collection Service), copy furnished the Regional Director having jurisdiction over their respective Districts, a Consolidated Report (Annex D) on each District Office's accomplishments under Operation "Even Returns" on or before Monday, September 8, 1997.

V. EFFECTIVITY

This Order shall take effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: All Regional Directors and Revenue District Officers
Original Law.To: Clarifications on the Implementation of RR No. 4-97 and RMO No. 19-97 on the Acceptable Modes of Payment

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVE

This Office recognizes that a number of taxpayers have requested that they be allowed to pay their taxes through check payments, citing various reasons for this appeal.

In the interest of the taxpaying public, this Revenue Memorandum Order authorizing the relaxation of the requirements of RMO NO. 19-97 is promulgated, in consideration of the following:

1. To facilitate the payment of taxes by taxpayers who would like to avail of the Acceptable Modes of Payment, but are unable to do so, at this time; and

2. To clearly define the limits of the case-to-case extension of the deadline for the compliance of all taxpayers with the mandate of RMO No. 19-97.

II. POLICIES AND GUIDELINES

In acceding to requests of taxpayers that they be allowed to pay their taxes using check payments, the policies and guidelines below must be followed:

1. Requests must be addressed to the Revenue District Officer having jurisdiction over the concerned taxpayer's Home RDO.

2. Requests of those taxpayers who are experiencing some difficulties in complying with RR No. 4-97 and RMO No. 19-97 must be thoroughly evaluated by the Revenue District Officer concerned, to determine the legitimacy of their requests.

Any request for payment through checks must be acted upon by the Revenue District Officer concerned, within the same working day such request was received.

3. Taxpayers who are requesting that they be allowed to pay through checks, but have already enrolled and are paying their taxes under the Bank Debit System, shall not be allowed to revert to their erstwhile mode of payment.

However, requests filed by those Taxpayers who shall be enrolling and paying their taxes for the first time since the implementation of RMO No. 19-97, shall be acted upon.

4. Taxpayers whose requests for payment through checks are granted should, however, be encouraged to enroll with their chosen Authorized Agent Bank, the soonest possible time, and to give their check payments directly to said AAB. The AAB, in turn, must issue the corresponding official receipt for such check payment.

Check payments must not be received by any official or employee of any Regional or District Office, with the exception of manager's checks or cashier's checks issued by non-accredited banks within those municipalities where there are no AABs. Said manager's checks or cashier's checks may be accepted only by the Revenue Collection Agent assigned thereat.

5. A Taxpayer's authorized agent/representative (e.g. an accounting firm, legal consultant or any other person or entity with a special power or authority for such purpose) shall be allowed to file the Taxpayer's TRU Form and required documents in his/her behalf. The agent/representative shall, however, be liable to make tax payments in behalf of their client, using the appropriate mode of payment.

6. The period of extension shall be in effect only until Tuesday, September 30, 1997. No further requests shall be entertained after this date. Taxpayers whose requests were granted under the guidelines set forth in this Order, must be reminded by the Revenue District Officer concerned, of the lapse of the extension period at least five (5) working days before the actual deadline.

III. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

All Revenue District Officers must provide the Office of the Commissioner, copy furnished the Deputy Commissioner, Operations Group, a weekly Report (format attached as Annex A) on taxpayers requesting for extensions, the reasons to justify such requests, and the action taken by the Revenue District Officer.

IV. EFFECTIVITY

This Order takes effect immediately.

LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue
